theorem.justification: This theorem gives the exact finite algorithmic answer to the design-frontier question and states the sharp worst-case limitation of certified pruning.
theorem.gap: Finite validated searches admit sound pruning, but the frozen model supplies no monotonicity theorem that forces a strict reduction from exhaustive evaluation.
theorem.consumer: It returns the finite menu of nondominated certified prospective designs while preserving undecided candidates as noncertified.

added_lemmas.justification: This is the precise relative completeness counterpart to the unconditional finite-termination and one-sided-soundness theorem.
added_lemmas.gap: Finite interval procedures need not certify at fixed controls; eventual success follows only from strict exact slack and uniform convergence of every enclosure and mesh used by the return rule.
added_lemmas.consumer: It explains when increasing declared numerical controls will eventually turn a genuinely separated prospective design into a certified one, without asserting that either synthetic benchmark qualifies.

prose_updates.tldr: Known linearly independent raw-count compositions recover unrestricted labeled type laws for arbitrary \(p\geq1\) by a logarithmic count-PGF inverse, with positive Poisson aliases proving necessity. Any recovered count-valued law in the published pairwise-identifiable CPCM class then has its labeled DAG identified; intervention contrasts and validation use the stricter compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass. For \(p\geq3\), the headline is a finite sound tri-valued certifier: it always terminates, and only a \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output verifies a rational chart-projection cover together with wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local Jacobian nonsingularity, interiority, PGF-tail, and designated-contrast precision bounds. The finite-grid theorem separately proves existence of some finite rational grid and cover with positive exact margins; it does not certify either prescribed synthetic input. Pointwise sample-split Wald inference is conditional on certification, the capped certified-design frontier is finite, and the three-node base/conditional-refinement benchmark status remains open.

project_justification.gap: Transform inversion, direct-law CPCM identification, and validated numerics are established separately. The published CPCM result starts from a direct count-valued joint law and does not recover labeled type laws through known multi-composition pools; existing validated-numerics results do not jointly propagate infinite-support PGF tails through graph exclusion, remote within-graph separation, local chart injectivity, Jacobian regularity, covariance, and intervention precision.
project_justification.niche: Prospective known-composition designs need a proof-producing bridge from aggregate raw-count laws to labeled cellular laws and then to the broadest justified graph class, with intervention and inference claims explicitly confined to a compact certifiable polynomial subclass.
project_justification.fill: The project composes the arbitrary-dimensional rank frontier with published pairwise-identifiable CPCM DAG recovery, proves causal minimality of the strict positive-polynomial benchmark directly from its positive edge coefficients, and supplies for \(p\geq3\) an always-terminating one-sided-sound certifier plus a finite capped design frontier. Relative eventual certification is proved only under explicit strict exact slack and uniform convergence of all numerical controls; no prescribed synthetic input is claimed to meet those premises.

prose_updates.related_work: Shih--Hero is credited for logarithmic transform inversion of independent additive components; the integer-multiplicity multivariate count-PGF recovery map and positive unrestricted converse are derived here. Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin Definitions 9--10 describe the causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM setting, and their direct-law DAG result is composed with labeled unpooling here. The positive-polynomial Poisson subclass is shown, edge by edge, to be causally minimal and pairwise identifiable rather than acquiring those properties by definition. Carrasco--Florens and Newey--McFadden supply finite-moment minimum-distance ingredients. Rump, Kearfott, and Berz--Makino motivate validated arithmetic, interval global search, and Taylor enclosures. The new validation step jointly carries analytic Poisson-PGF tails through wrong-graph exclusion, the corrected one-sided remote-subset branch, rational chart covers, Jacobian and covariance checks, and designated causal precision. Its relative eventual-certification theorem is conditional on strict exact slack and convergent controls, not an assertion about the two fixed synthetic runs.
prose_updates.interpretation: Full column rank first identifies each labeled cellular observational law; it does not define a graph or an intervention. The recovered law identifies a labeled DAG on the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class. Intervention contrasts require the narrower causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass, whose full support identifies the kernels in the truncated factorization. The certificate handle enumerates the declared finite design class, records all three statuses, and promotes only \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) inputs to the Pareto comparison. Fixed controls always terminate but can remain undecided. Along a control sequence, eventual certification follows only from the separately stated strict-slack and uniform-convergence hypotheses.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The leaf ceiling and outward-rounded operation bound are unconditional finite ceilings, not efficiency guarantees. The \(27\)-point floating-point pilot and its two pointwise Jacobian singular values certify neither compact-box graph separation nor remote identification, chart coverage, tails, covariance, or useful contrast precision. Compactness converts strict exact slack into eventual positivity of sufficiently accurate lower enclosures, and the corrected remote rule permits a boundary-straddling box to pass from positive moment distance alone. That result is relative: without the stipulated strict margins and convergent truncation, Taylor, subdivision, and rounding controls, the procedure may return \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\). Neither fixed synthetic input currently has a validated proof object.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Unrestricted rank recovery and stability apply for arbitrary \(p\geq1\). Labeled-DAG transfer applies to recovered laws in the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable count-valued CPCM class and imposes no Poisson source law. Intervention contrasts, finite-grid construction, certification, and Wald inference are confined to the compact causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass and, for the designated contrasts, require \(p\geq3\) and fixed \(\iota\). Certification is always terminating and one-sided sound but may be undecided. Eventual certification is conditional on strict positive exact graph, remote, chart, Jacobian, interiority, algebraic, and precision margins together with uniform numerical convergence; it certifies neither prescribed benchmark by itself. Covariance and Wald claims additionally require normalized strictly positive row fractions and give pointwise, not uniform post-selection, coverage. No claim covers unknown thinning, normalization, composition error, shared-well dependence, hidden types, high-dimensional growth, or biologically calibrated coefficient boxes.

statement_notes.justification: The proposition now proves full support, causal sufficiency, and causal minimality directly; each positive polynomial edge changes a positive-probability conditional Poisson kernel, and the nonexceptional increasing rate verifies the maintained pairwise condition.
statement_notes.gap: The published CPCM definitions do not themselves verify causal minimality or pairwise identifiability for this paper's strict positive-polynomial benchmark.
statement_notes.consumer: It validates that every graph and parameter box searched by the reusable certificate lies inside the broader direct-law identifiable CPCM class.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem proves unconditional finite termination and one-sided soundness of every certified or refuted output. The separate \(\mathrm{thm{:}relative\text{-}eventual\text{-}certification}\) supplies the only completeness statement, under explicit strict slack and convergent controls.
statement_notes.gap: Existing validated-numerics results do not jointly propagate Poisson-PGF tails through wrong-graph, remote-subset, local-chart, covariance, and causal-precision tasks, and fixed finite controls need not decide them.
statement_notes.consumer: It turns a declared prospective design into an auditable go, stop, or undecided result, while the relative companion theorem states exactly when refinement eventually yields go.
